Transfusion: Predict the Next Token and Diffuse Images (NeurIPS 2024) • Proposes a unified training framework combining autoregressive language modeling with diffusion-based image generation. • Uses a shared transformer backbone to support both reasoning and high-quality image synthesis. • Demonstrates improved image generation guided by textual understanding. Research Gaps & Limitations • Training requires extremely large-scale multimodal datasets and computational resources. • Dual-objective optimization increases architectural and training complexity. • Inference latency remains high due to diffusion-based decoding. • Evaluation is mainly limited to text–image tasks, excluding audio and video modalities. • The approach does not explicitly address multimodal hallucination or grounding errors. While Transfusion advances unification, its efficiency and scalability constraints limit practical deployment. 2. 3. Gemini: A Family of Highly Capable Multimodal Models (Google DeepMind, 2024) • Presents a large-scale multimodal foundation model capable of processing text, image, audio, and video inputs. • Employs early multimodal fusion and joint pretraining for strong cross-modal reasoning. • Achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple multimodal benchmarks. Research Gaps & Limitations • Requires massive TPU-scale infrastructure, limiting reproducibility. • The model architecture and training details are partially abstracted. • Closed-source nature restricts academic experimentation and benchmarking. • Ethical and bias mitigation strategies are not quantitatively evaluated. • Deployment on resource-constrained environments is not feasible. Gemini demonstrates strong multimodal capabilities but remains inaccessible for open research and deployment. 4. Towards Artificial General Intelligence via a Multimodal Foundation Model (Nature Communications 2023) • Proposes a multimodal foundation model trained on large-scale image–text data. • Demonstrates emergent reasoning capabilities across vision and language tasks. • Suggests multimodal learning as a path toward general intelligence. Research Gaps & Limitations • Limited to image–text modalities, excluding audio and video. • Does not support diffusion-based generative modeling. • Requires massive pretraining data and computational resources. • Reasoning capabilities are evaluated on a limited set of benchmarks. • Lacks explicit mechanisms for grounding and hallucination control.

PaLM-E: An Embodied Multimodal Language Model (ICML 2023) • Introduces an embodied multimodal language model that integrates vision, language, and robot sensor data. • Injects continuous visual and state representations directly into a large language model for embodied reasoning. • Demonstrates strong performance on robotic manipulation, planning, and visual question answering tasks.

Research Gaps & Limitations • The model requires extremely large-scale computational resources, making it difficult to reproduce. • Performance heavily depends on high-quality robot-specific training data. • The approach focuses mainly on robotics and does not generalize well to non-embodied multimodal generation tasks. • Long-horizon planning is still constrained by errors from low-level policies. • Real-time deployment and safety in dynamic environments are not thoroughly addressed. PaLM-E establishes strong embodied multimodal reasoning but remains computationally expensive and domain-restricted. 6. KOSMOS-2: Grounding Multimodal Large Language Models to the World (arXiv / Microsoft Research, 2023) • Proposes a multimodal large language model with explicit grounding between text and image regions. • Introduces location tokens and grounding-aware training data to link language with visual objects. • Demonstrates improved performance on visual grounding, referring expression, and grounded image captioning tasks.
